**Architecture And Separation Of Concerns**
The dependency satisfaction helper lives in the domain layer at [crates/jit/src/domain/types.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/domain/types.rs:117). The main consumers I checked route through it: `Issue::is_blocked`, `query_blocked`, transition blockers, output unmet rendering, and dependency-add demotion. `claim_next` uses `query_ready` at [crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs:1088). No boundary violation found.

**Functional Correctness**
Rejected dependencies are treated as met in the core implementation paths and are covered by focused tests in [crates/jit/tests/dependency_met_tests.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/tests/dependency_met_tests.rs:20). However, REQ-4 is not fully satisfied because stale comments/docs still describe the old Done-only or incomplete-dependency model.

**Tests And Gates**
I did not rerun cargo tests because the issue has a passed `cargo-ci` gate. Recorded evidence shows `cargo-ci` passed with exit code 0 on 2026-07-09. I did run `./scripts/jit-validate.sh`; it passed.

**Prior Review Feedback**
The prior failed review asked for stale dependency wording to be swept. Some locations were fixed, but the issue remains in command docs/comments and user-facing docs.

**Correctness And Invariants**
No new atomic-write, event logging, gate-semantics, assignee/label format, PID-safety, unsafe-code, or error-handling violation found in the reviewed dependency-met changes.

**CLI Contract**
No missing `--json` support found in the reviewed surfaces.

**Documentation**
Documentation is the blocking area: the implementation docs mostly state the terminal-state rule, but stale Done-only and “incomplete dependencies” wording remains.

1. [crates/jit/src/commands/dependency.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/commands/dependency.rs:582) still says batch dependency add “demotes it when any newly-added dependency isn’t `Done`.” That directly contradicts REQ-4’s terminal-state rule because a `Rejected` dependency is also met and must not demote a ready issue. Severity: medium.
2. Stale user-facing/docs wording from the prior review remains: [docs/reference/cli-commands.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/cli-commands.md:1394) says claims are blocked behind “incomplete dependencies,” [docs/reference/cli-commands.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/cli-commands.md:2444) says removing the last “incomplete dependency” unblocks, [docs/how-to/troubleshooting.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/troubleshooting.md:32) shows the same stale phrasing, and [crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs:1563) repeats it in a test comment. This leaves the prior review feedback unresolved. Severity: low.
